I was reading this article earlier, and it got me thinking. If aliens could respond, then their technology must be at around the same development. We have only developed radio technology in the past century, an insanely small fraction in the history of our evolution. And even if the aliens have developed this tech, then we are assuming that they haven't progressed beyond this method of communication. Hell, that's if they even used radio waves at any point, and not some other bizarre way of chatting.

Additionally, they have little to no incentive to provide any sort of help. Anything that our civilization may produce would surely be of no use to a species that can rapidly travel through space. Even if we had valuable elements that are exclusive to Earth (gold comes to mind, being malleable and conductive) that they could use, I doubt they would be willing to travel millions of miles to get it. Just because a species is more advanced than us, doesn't mean that they don't have their own shit going on.

I don't believe that we are alone in the universe, and I would be trilled to talk to an intelligent being from another planet. I just think that either they wouldn't be able to respond, or just straight up wouldn't want to.

*I had this for the very first time at a night noodle market the other day. I work with a few Pinoy's and they'd told be the check it out. After a 45 minute wait in line (by which I figured that it must be REALLY good cause no one was complaining about the wait), I tasted on of the most awesome char grilled BBQ flavours I've ever had. And I've eaten a LOT of BBQ, being Australian as I am. (Read - literally every other day, rain, hail or shine...)

The recipe below was pulled off the web but isn't unique - and like all BBQ - play with it till it suits your taste I guess.

~~ Code*

Ingredients

2 lbs pork belly (skin removed), butt, or shoulder; cut into desired sizes
1 head garlic; crushed
1/2 cup soy sauce
1/2 cup banana or tomato ketchup
1/4 cup 7-up or sprite soda
3 tablespoons lemon (calamansi) juice or vinegar
1/4 tablespoon ground black pepper
3 tablespoons brown sugar
2 tablespoons peanut butter
Bamboo skewers (pre-soaked in water for about 30 minutes)

Cooking Instructions

Mix all ingredients in a bowl and set aside in the refrigerator for at least 24 hours.

Skew the pork, then grill over charcoal or gas grill.

Baste using the remaining marinade sauce while grilling.

Cook until done.

Eat.

Notes

Common ingredients for Pinoy barbecue marinade are: soy sauce, garlic, banana ketchup, citrus fruit juice (calamansi or lemon) or vinegar, sugar, and ground pepper, where the outcome of the final taste should be sweet-sour-salty at same time. Additional list of ingredients for variation includes soda (7-up, sprite, and moutain dew), beer, onion, peanut butter, and salt. Dipping sauce ingredients for this dish includes vinegar, minced garlic and onion, and salt and pepper.
